title: Quiz — Thursday night, and the train is climbing
learning_goal: Know how the mail for India crossed the Alps before 1871, and feel how new the way through is.

narration.script: It is Thursday night, and the train is climbing. Two years before Fogg, how did this train get to the other side of the Alps?
narration.after_script: Over the top. Seventy-seven kilometres of railway beside the mountain road, and about five hours. In 1867 you crossed these mountains in the open air. In 1872 you slept through them.

overlays.text: Two years before Fogg: how did this train cross the Alps?
overlays.note: THE ONLY OVERLAY ON THIS SCENE. This scene has no media, so the player draws its own card from title + learning_goal + overlays — and sceneCard() prints every overlay's text at once, ignoring at_s. A caption naming the Mont Cenis Pass Railway would therefore sit on screen from second zero and hand the traveller the answer (R5). The 77 km / 2,283 m / 1-in-11 figures live in the correct option's feedback, where they are the reward.

interaction.prompt: Two years before Fogg, how did this train get to the other side of the Alps?

options.text: Everyone changed to a coach in summer, and a sledge in winter
options.feedback: True until 1868 — and it is why crossing the Alps was a story people told for the rest of their lives.

options.text: A railway laid along the mountain road over the pass, gripping a third rail in the middle
options.feedback: Seventy-seven kilometres over the top, a summit at 2,283 metres, gradients of one in eleven, about five hours — and the mail for India went over it.

options.text: The carriages were carried through a tunnel on flat wagons
options.feedback: There was no tunnel yet. That is what the next few minutes are about.

transition.out: cut to the Fell train, then the works
transition.music_cue: none; no sting on the opening date

production_notes: SEGMENT 5, first third (45 s of 215; segment fill 75 % — the chapter maximum — and a 385-word ceiling, of which this scene spends 57). QUIZ FIRST so the Fell railway is a discovery rather than a lecture. NO MEDIA ENTRIES, deliberately: the player's quiz branch shows media[0] of kind image the instant the scene opens, and the only honest picture for this question — M-240, the Fell train — is the ANSWER. The rundown asks for M-240 'in the feedback', which the player cannot do (feedback is text), so M-240 opens the NEXT scene instead, at 0-10 s, under a caption naming the Fell railway: the answer image lands about two seconds after the reveal is spoken, which is as close to the rundown's intent as the engine allows. With no media the player draws its own scene card from `title` + `learning_goal` + overlays, so all three are written spoiler-free (R5: no wording from the correct option appears in the two minutes before it). The 'one in eleven' gradient and the summit height are on the caption and are not read aloud (R3).
